subject: Data retention exception — recap & next steps

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>

Date: Sat, 28 Feb 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Data retention exception — recap & next steps

Alex / Priya — thanks again for taking the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment.

Call highlights:
- Acme needs a path to process customer transcripts and extracted metadata without retaining PII in logs.
- Preferred outcome: "0-retention" for any transcript containing PII; limited operational logs retained only for troubleshooting.
- Must support data residency in the EU for EU tenant data; some production traffic will be global.
- Procurement/legal asked for amendments to the DPA and an explicit retention schedule for logs and metrics.

What Redwood can offer (high level):
1) Hosted API: configurable logging options — we can disable transcript storage for certain routes and only retain aggregated metrics.
2) Dedicated/Private: per-tenant retention schedules and custom redaction at ingress (recommended if strict 0-retention is required).
3) Operational logs: support for shortened retention windows (e.g., 30 days for metadata-only logs) and the option to push logs to a customer-controlled S3/Kafka for audit.

Attachments: initial proposal draft and SOC2 summary attached for your review.

Next steps I propose:
- Redwood to produce an updated proposal with an explicit retention schedule and sample DPA language (due: 1 week).
- Rafael will outline the technical design for ingress redaction and ephemeral transcript handling.
- Schedule follow-up call next week to review legal language and run through technical Qs — suggest Thu 2026-03-05 10:00 AM PT.

If that works, we’ll kick off the proposal + legal draft and loop in your procurement contact.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Data retention exception — recap & next steps

Hi Camila — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side before you draft the DPA language:

1) 0-retention: We need the option to have transcripts containing PII never written to long-term storage. If this is achievable only on Dedicated/Private deployments, please state that clearly.
2) Operational logs: We need to retain some level of request metadata for incident investigation (request ID, timestamp, model used) but without any transcript text. Target: 30 days metadata retention, after which the metadata must be purged.
3) Redaction: If Redwood offers client-side redaction or pre-ingest redaction hooks, that would be preferred.
4) Data residency: EU tenant traffic MUST remain in EU region (GDPR).

Can you also share a sample clause for: (a) deletion confirmation (log that a record was deleted and a deletion audit for 12 months), and (b) exceptions/escrows for law enforcement requests? Procurement will want the exact wording.

Priya (security) — will you join the follow-up call?

Thanks,
Alex
Sr. Product Manager — Platform
Acme Corp

Hey Alex / Camila — Rafael from Solutions here, jumping in with a technical breakdown and proposed approaches for the retention requirements.

Short answers up front:
- 0-retention for transcripts with PII is feasible, but the recommended deployment model is Dedicated or Private (hosted API can support limited use-cases via ingress redaction and ephemeral processing).
- Operational metadata-only logs (request ID, timestamp, model id, latency, error codes) are straightforward to retain for 30 days; we can configure automatic purge jobs.
- For EU residency we can pin processing to EU regions and ensure logs for EU tenants remain in EU storage.

Recommended implementation options:
A) Dedicated/Private (strongest guarantee):
  - Per-tenant retention policy enforced at the storage layer.
  - Option to disable transcript persistence entirely and only write ephemeral KV caches to local GPU memory.
  - Customer-managed KMS for key separation.

B) Hosted (fastest):
  - Ingress redaction hooks: Redwood provides a middleware hook that applies regex/ML redaction before ingestion.
  - Ephemeral mode: transcripts processed and discarded immediately; we retain a 30-day metadata index if requested (configurable).
  - Caveat: exactly-zero retention for transcripts that were logged in live debugging windows may require additional operational controls; we recommend a canary + test period.

Audit and deletion evidence:
- We can produce deletion confirmations and an audit log (delete event id, timestamp, initiating principal). We can retain deletion audit metadata for 12 months as you requested.
- For law-enforcement exceptions, Redwood follows the process in our DPA; we can add explicit escalation and notification SLAs in the DPA draft.

Next steps from us:
- I’ll attach a short technical note (ingress-redaction-design.md) outlining redaction hooks and configuration examples.
- Camila will lead on the contractual language and proposal.

Happy to discuss on the follow-up call — if Priya can make it, I can do a short demo of the ingress-redaction flow.

— Rafael
